expl.summary: Every jet is placed on 16 neurons, each a clipped sum of if-statements on jet observables, and each class score adds some neurons and subtracts others; this formula was tuned toward the network's decision for each jet and reaches a validation accuracy of 80.3%. Jet mass is its main ingredient: most neurons are built from mass thresholds between 62.6 and 172.8 GeV. The g score adds the particle-count neuron 1 (+36%), on which gluon jets sit far above all other jets (7.84 against at most 3.68), and the low-mass neuron 9 (+18%), and it subtracts neuron 4 for jets with a mass of roughly 74-144 GeV and low D₂ (-20%). The q score subtracts neuron 4 (-36%) and neuron 1 (-16%) and adds neuron 9 (+29%), on which quark jets sit highest (4.39). The W and Z scores both subtract neuron 8 for wide, massive jets with pT at ΔR 0.2-0.4 (-26% and -28%) and add neuron 5 for pT carried by the 50 hardest particles (+12% and +14%).
